doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Future work around New Orleans
summary: Casual work, substitute gigs and session calls for Jazzology and GHB.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Cool. What’s in the future as far as — you’re joining a band down there, any other opportunities in surrounding New Orleans?

Yeah. There’s a lot of casual work, parties, weddings, things like that, and substitute work. You know some of the places go five days a week. One of the clubs has a shift of three bands on weekends. And sometimes people just get burned out and they want time off. Or they’re going on vacation or something like that. So if I’m there I’ll get a call. And recording work too. One of the labels I’ve done extensive recording for, Jazzology and GHB, it’s based in New Orleans. And when I lived there before, I got the first call as a session drummer. So I would imagine I’ll get that again.
